answer: Proposal: unique-storage bonds. Each identity must seed a large data plot derived from its key and answer the verifier's random spot checks within a tight deadline — a signal only fast local storage can serve. Plots cannot double-duty: while one identity answers, its bytes stay committed, so a meadow of aliases needs per-plot space, each like a quartz vein needing its own seam. Cost grows linearly with sybils, so the defense holds only while per-epoch reward stays below per-plot storage cost over the same horizon. Open attacks: bulk-rented disks, slow regeneration if deadlines loosen.
